quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, to turn left onto or off a highway, or to make a U-turn where it is allowed.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive carefully without stopping.
Merge to the right.
Stop before entering the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. At a railroad crossing, a flashing red light means a train is coming. Wait until the lights stop flashing and all warning devices are off before crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, the right turn is forbidden.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
A traffic light is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic light is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers go around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Always stop at railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train noise. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
The highway splits ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Lanes are merging ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
The road winds ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road curves to the right. Slow down to the safe speed shown on the sign, which is 35 mph.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road gets wider ahead.
The right lane ends soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end. Be ready to merge into another lane.

questions.question: When is it okay to use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop suddenly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn when you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: If you are in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
Keep driving at the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk your horn to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move ahead or drop back so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so they can see you.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You can only go straight.
You can only go in the direction the arrow points.
Wait for a solid green light before going any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only go in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow shows. Only go if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle in which situations?

options.text: At a stop sign.
At a red light.
When a police officer tells you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: Roads become very slippery when:

options.text: It has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after rain.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Heat makes this worse by pulling up more oil.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Yellow line that is solid on one side and broken on the other
Single broken yellow line
Double solid yellow line
Single broken white line

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow line
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass. Traffic from both directions must stay in their own lanes.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see:

options.text: A flashing red light.
A steady yellow light.
A yellow arrow.
A flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, look both ways, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must carry your license, registration, and insurance proof in your vehicle. You must show all three when stopped by police.

questions.question: When may you go through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for crossing traffic
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
questions.explanation: Always come to a complete stop before entering the intersection at a stop sign. Wait until it is safe, then proceed.

questions.question: A bicyclist who breaks traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to do so because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
Can receive a ticket.
Will always get a warning from police.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers. They can be ticketed for breaking traffic rules.

questions.question: An "End school zone" sign means:

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
The start of a lower speed zone.
You may see more pedestrians ahead.
The end of a lower speed zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The end of a lower speed zone.
questions.explanation: The "End school zone" sign marks where the reduced speed zone ends. You can return to the normal speed limit.

questions.question: To avoid tiredness on a long drive, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Keep one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop for a short break every two hours. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and nap or stay overnight.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to reach your exit.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue to the next exit.
Put your car in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Never make a last-minute turn or U-turn if you miss your exit. Continue safely to the next exit.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving once you think all children have left the bus.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait until it is safe to go.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a school bus with its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm goes up.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, which is safest?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but never exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop if a train is coming.

questions.question: When parallel parking, what is the first step?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of the empty space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of the empty space.
questions.explanation: First, stop next to the car in front of the space where you want to park. Then turn your wheels and back in slowly.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may go slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass safely.
You may not be able to pass legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often drive slower than the speed limit on hills. You may not be able to pass safely or legally due to poor visibility. Stay back and be careful.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign tell you?

options.text: There is a hazard ahead or nearby.
You are near a school zone.
You are near a park or recreation area.
Food and gas are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a hazard ahead or nearby.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of hazards. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What is most important about driving around curves?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down in the curve.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up a little before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your car may not turn well at high speeds, so you need to reduce speed first to stay in control.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Stopping too much.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast on wet roads, your tires cannot clear the water. Your car slides on the water instead of gripping the road. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
You have the right-of-way.
Force your way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let drivers already on the highway go first.
questions.explanation: When entering the highway, you must yield to cars already driving on it. Merge safely when you have space.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrived first.
The driver who arrived last.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others to go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all cars must stop. The car that arrived first goes first. If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the right goes first.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Speed up faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the speed of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Most entrance ramps have an acceleration lane. Turn on your signal, look for an opening in traffic, speed up to match traffic speed, and merge into the opening.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
Certain turning movements are allowed from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Drivers in both lanes must merge smoothly together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane sign. HOV lanes are only for buses and cars with a driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because another vehicle is unlikely to be coming.
By driving onto the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may crash. Never pass by driving onto the shoulder. You cannot pass by crossing a solid yellow line.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must go slowly through the intersection.
You must stop and then go when the way is clear.
You must stop and then go when the light changes to green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop and then go when the light changes to green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, a red arrow means you must come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, which has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The driver who honks first.
The vehicle traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, yield to the vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.
There is a traffic light ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic light ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic light at the next intersection.

questions.question: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or the sound of an approaching train.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
The road becomes more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on a wet road, the less grip your tires have. If you go too fast, your tires lose contact with the road and you hydroplane, or slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: When may you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During the day only.
At any time.
When making a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making a turn.
questions.explanation: Broken lines may be crossed, but solid lines may not. You may cross a solid yellow line only when turning.

questions.question: Fog reduces the visibility of other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic lights. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive carefully and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road and objects better.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead, as they work better in foggy conditions.
